Ruim 46 jaar lang draait Vredestein op s: For a good 46 years Vredestein runs on students. Mr Blooij was a plumber by trade and did a lot of the work on the building himself. Maxim groeide op in Driebergen. Na zijn: Maxim grew up in Driebergen. After his divorce he stayed connected to the neighbourhood for his children and bought a building close to his parental home. He saw the size, the space and the barn. As a former IVA student he liked the idea of keeping this student house going. Manon swapped Amsterdam and the sea for the Utrechtse Heuvelrug. She misses the beach, but now works in Culemborg and has quietly become a fan.
De villa was in de jaren zeventig rigour: The villa was radically rebuilt in the seventies: cherry wood everywhere, cartwheels worked into the walls and bronze door handles that fell off as soon as you opened them. The ground floor was rotten and we removed the crawl space for an industrial concrete poured floor, insulated with clay granules and then planed into a beautiful industrial base. On the upper floors we are working with a burnt pine floor and bringing the panels back to their former glory. The ornamental plasterwork had unfortunately disappeared and we solved that with chandeliers. We do want to bring back the awnings, the French doors and the leaded-glass windows. Through contact with the Roelofsen family we got the chance in 2022 to see a great many photos from before the radical seventies renovation. We were able to invite the whole family and heard all the childhood stories: sliding down the banister, the barn parties and the communal kitchen with the coal stove. The most valuable photo we have ever seen of this house. There is still contact and they like to follow the renovation of their childhood home.
Oktober 2020, Maxim ontvangt de sleutels: October 2020, Maxim receives the keys to Hoofdstraat 147
Van kelder tot zolder gestript en opnieu: Stripped from cellar to attic and rebuilt. 15 cm insulation, fully plastered, underfloor heating in the concrete poured floor and air conditioning on the upper floors. All electrics and plumbing renewed. From 11 rooms to 7, with 3 bathrooms, two kitchens, a kitchenette and a gym.
Elke ruimte werd teruggestript naar de b: Every space was stripped back to the basics. The walls were given 15 centimetres of insulation and then completely re-plastered. Underfloor heating was installed in the industrial concrete poured floor on the ground floor. On the second and third floors there are air conditioners: the front of the house faces the sun directly and heats up considerably in summer. In the past residents planted linden trees in front of the door for shade. We chose an open garden with a view of the street. All the electrics have been renewed and brought up to modern requirements. The same goes for the plumbing. Mr Blooij was a plumber and had stuck a lot together himself over the years. The overall picture had been lost: when digging we found gas pipes in the garden and other dangerous connections. Everything has been made safe and laid again. The aim remains to bring the house back to its former glory, but to modern standards of sustainability and climate.

De Hoofdstraat van Driebergen zoals hij: The Hoofdstraat of Driebergen as it looked around 1910. Fewer cars, more peace. Villa Vredestein is on the right, recognisable by the characteristic roof and the bay window.
De Dorpsstraat van Driebergen, begin twi: The Dorpsstraat of Driebergen, early twentieth century
The Dorpsstraat of Driebergen around 1910. A man with his bicycle, rails in the middle of the road, tall villas on either side. The calm and dignity of Driebergen breathe from every detail of this card.
Vroeg twintigste-eeuwse ansichtkaart van: Early twentieth-century postcard of the Hoofdweg
De Driebergse Hoofdweg in sepia, vermoed: The Driebergen Hoofdweg in sepia, probably around 1905–1915. The tram rails are still present, the buildings recognisable. On the left the start of the Villa Vredestein plot.
Portretansichtkaart van het pension aan: Portrait postcard of the guesthouse on the Hoofdstraat
Een verticale ansichtkaart met voluit de: A vertical postcard with the full text 'Pension Villa Vredestein, Driebergen'. The villa in its best clothes, full of ivy, elegant and inviting. This is how the guesthouse presented itself to the outside world.
Vroege ansichtkaart van de villa zelf: Early postcard of the villa itself
Een vroege ansichtkaart met het opschrif: An early postcard with the inscription 'Vredestein, Driebergen'. The villa looks even barer than now, the planting still had years to grow. But the contours are unmistakably the same as today.
Het pand aangeduid als rustoord aan de D: The building referred to as a rest home on the Dorpstraat
Opschrift: 'Driebergen, Dorpstraat met R: Inscription: 'Driebergen, Dorpstraat with Rustoord Vredestein'. Over the years the building was also referred to as a rest home, a resting point along the Heuvelrug. A reminder of the many forms this house has taken in a century.
Een van de vroegste bekende foto's van d: One of the earliest known photos of the villa

One of the earliest known photos of the villa, taken around 1910. The façade is unfortunately no longer identical to how it looks now. We would love to restore the bargeboard to its former glory. The veranda at the front is gone, as are the leaded-glass windows and the casement windows. We are very happy with photos like this to see how it was, and to know what we are working towards.
De voorkant in de jaren '60-'70, voor de: The front in the '60s–'70s, before the fatal renovation
Zo zag de voorkant eruit in de jaren dat: This is what the front looked like in the years when the Roelofsen family lived here, the sixties or seventies. This is before the fatal renovation in which all the glass and lead was replaced. The veranda with French doors is still present here, as are the casement windows. The fire escape on the side is not there yet either. The bargeboard of the façade had already been removed by then.
Het personeel van het christelijk pensio: The staff of the Christian guesthouse Vredestein

The staff of the Christian guesthouse Vredestein, in the time of the Roelofsen family. We received this photo from them. They stand here so familiarly, as if they are about to go back inside to make tea for the guests.
De achtertuin zoals die er uitzag in het: The back garden as it looked in the Roelofsen era
De achtertuin in de tijd van het pension: The back garden in the time of the guesthouse. No vegetable garden, but a neat ornamental garden that suited a respectable lodging address. Now it has become a wilder, livelier place.
Maxim ontvangt de sleutels van Hoofdstra: Maxim receives the keys to Hoofdstraat 147
Oktober 2020. Maxim ontvangt de sleutels: October 2020. Maxim receives the keys to Hoofdstraat 147. Behind him a road of searching and letting go. Ahead of him: years of work, and a place he holds on to this time.
De aankondiging van het nieuwe hoofdstuk: The announcement of the new chapter, October 2020
The announcement of the new chapter, in October 2020. A moving card with address, date and the promise of an open door. We are still keeping that promise.
Historische blauwdruk-kadasterkaart van: Historic blueprint land registry map of Driebergen-Rijsenburg
In het Nationaal Archief liggen de blauw: The National Archives hold the blueprint maps of Driebergen from the early twentieth century. Every plot neatly drawn in, including Hoofdstraat 147, even then a remarkably large lot.
Tweede blauwdrukkaart van het gebied ron: Second blueprint map of the area around Driebergen-Rijsenburg
Een tweede blauwdrukkaart van hetzelfde: A second blueprint map of the same area. Together they give a complete picture of what Driebergen looked like a century ago, street by street, plot by plot.
Perceelkaart met bouwnummers 2253-2256,: Plot map with building numbers 2253-2256, Hoofdstraat 147
Bouwnummers 2253 tot 2256. Op dit stuk p: Building numbers 2253 to 2256. On this piece of paper is the legal identity of the villa: metres, boundaries, ownership. Dry to look at, but behind every number is a story.
Historische bebouwingskaart langs de Hoo: Historic site map along the Hoofdstraat
De Hoofdstraat in kaart gebracht. Je zie: The Hoofdstraat mapped out. You can see how dense the buildings already were, how narrow the plots, how little has changed in a hundred years in the layout of this part of Driebergen.
Handgeschreven archiefregister met ruimt: Handwritten archive register with room dimensions of Hfdstr. 147
Handgeschreven in het kadasterarchief: d: Handwritten in the land registry archive: the dimensions of every room of Hoofdstraat 147, once measured by an official with a ruler and ink. The villa is now exactly as large as stated here.
Tweede pagina, historische maatvoering v: Second page, historical dimensions of the building
The second page of the same register. Together they form an accurate picture of the layout of the villa, recorded on paper more than a century ago.
Officieel bouwregister met aantekeningen: Official building register with notes and construction dates
Het officiële bouwregister uit de archie: The official building register from the archives. It states when the villa was built, who the owner was and what the construction dates are. The beginning of the story in three lines of black ink.
Vervolg van het bouwregister, historisch: Continuation of the building register, historical layout
Het vervolg van het bouwregister, aanvul: The continuation of the building register: additions, corrections, notes. Documents like these are the backbone of the history of Villa Vredestein.
Zo zag het eruitzag toen we kochten, 202: This is what it looked like when we bought, 2020
De begane grond van Villa Vredestein in: The ground floor of Villa Vredestein in 2020: living room, kitchen, hall and two bedrooms. Quite a lot has since been moved around. The French doors at the back have been restored. The kitchen becomes our bedroom, the bedroom a bathroom, the bathroom a technical room for water pump and central heating. The two bedrooms have been added to the living room, which is now L-shaped, and the rear part has become an open kitchen with an island.
Zo zag de plattegrond eruit in 2020. De: This is what the floor plan looked like in 2020. The first floor has four bed-sitting rooms, a dining room, a hallway and a balcony at the front. This is the middle floor where our children now stay. The storage room and dining room are the last places in Vredestein that still need to be insulated. The storage room becomes a gym with a kitchenette, and the dining room a luxury bathroom with a bath.
Zo kochten we het huis, met extra badkam: This is how we bought the house, with an extra bathroom
Zo kochten we het huis in 2020, met een: This is how we bought the house in 2020, with an extra bathroom. That student bathroom contained 3,000 kg of reinforced concrete and was completely covered in mould. We demolished it first.
De bovenste verdieping anno 2020: vier z: The top floor in 2020: four bed-sitting rooms, a hallway, bathroom and storage room. This is the floor where the students live, each with their own room. From the bed-sitting-room hall we made a shared kitchen and living room. The toilet and storage room became a shared bathroom with toilet. In time we would like to create a separate entrance to this floor. The balcony is now used as an emergency exit.
De woonkamer zoals die er uitzag vóór de: The living room as it looked before the work
Zo zag de woonkamer eruit voordat Manon: This is what the living room looked like before Manon & Maxim rolled up their sleeves. Outdated finish, dated colours, but beneath it all: the same space, the same proportions, the same magic.
Het begin van de grote transformatie in: The start of the great transformation in 2020
Het begin was radicaal: alles eruit wat: The beginning was radical: everything out that could not stay. Demolition is an act of trust: you destroy something in the hope that what lies beneath is better. That turned out to be true.
Maanden isolatiewerk voor een energiezui: Months of insulation work for an energy-efficient building
Maanden van isolatiewerk. Muren, vloeren: Months of insulation work. Walls, floors, roofs, everything was layered and sealed. It is the invisible work you never see afterwards, but always feel on a cold winter evening.
Het herstelwerk aan de historische ramen: The restoration work on the historic windows
Het herstelwerk aan de ramen was precisi: The restoration of the windows was precision work. Glaziers worked for days on each window, colour by colour, lead by lead. The result can be seen in the light that now falls through the hall.
De houtkachel werd vakkundig geplaatst e: The wood stove was expertly placed and bricked in
Maxim heeft de houtkachel met eigen hand: Maxim placed and bricked in the wood stove with his own hands. 'Carpe Diem' is what he calls it, and he gave the living room that feeling straight away. Now the stove is the first thing people notice when they come in.
De originele kristallen kroonluchters we: The original crystal chandeliers were moved with care
De originele kristallen kroonluchters ko: The original crystal chandeliers could not stay up during the work. They were carefully dismantled, wrapped and stored, and after the restoration hung again in exactly the same place.
Bijzondere vondsten tijdens de verbouwin: Special finds during the renovation work
Tijdens het slopen kwamen er bijzondere: During demolition some special finds came to light: old coins, a letter, hidden decorative elements. Every renovation of an old building is a bit of archaeology.
De legdag van de gietvloer werd feesteli: The day the poured floor was laid was celebrated
De dag dat de gietvloer werd gelegd, wer: The day the poured floor was laid was celebrated. That sounds exaggerated, but anyone who has walked on sand for weeks will understand. It was a milestone in the restoration of the ground floor.
Het terras werd aangelegd en het perceel: The terrace was laid and the plot landscaped
Het terras en de tuin werden als laatste: The terrace and garden were tackled last. Laying tiles, planting, laying out the vegetable garden. After the inside, finally the outside too, and the whole became complete.
Samen aan de slag in het historische pan: Getting to work together in the historic building
Niet alles is uitbesteed. Manon & Maxim: Not everything was outsourced. Manon & Maxim built, painted, screwed and hauled themselves. It is their building in the most literal sense of the word, and you can see that in every room.

Villa Vredestein werd gebouwd als buiten: Villa Vredestein was built as a country residence for the mayor of Krimpen aan den IJssel. Since then the building has welcomed countless residents. From Christian guesthouse to student house, from renovation project to what it will become: a place to be proud of.
Achter de originele gevel schuilen hoge: Behind the original façade are high ceilings, an industrial poured floor downstairs and burnt pine upstairs. Original details are returning step by step: leaded-glass windows, French doors, wood stoves. Manon and Maxim live in the middle of it while the plan slowly takes shape.
